colour_space: all textures are linear data: import with sRGB off; colour comes from tints/gradients
frame_order: flipbooks start top-left and run row by row (Unity Texture Sheet Animation order)

Acid_Splash.channels: R lit shading (diffuse + highlight, premultiplied by alpha), G thickness, B specular only, A alpha
Acid_Splash.blend: Alpha blend premultiplied: rgb = lerp(acid dark, acid bright, G) * R + B * 0.6, emission = G * glow
Acid_Splash.tint: acid lime (0.55, 1, 0.15) to dark olive; a little emission on thick parts
Acid_Splash.notes: Pivot = splash origin (U 0.5, V 0.34 from the bottom). Camera-facing.

Beam_Core.notes: V across the beam, U along it; tile ~1 per beam width x4.

Beam_Noise.layout: single, tiles in U and V
Beam_Noise.channels: R energy filaments (stretched along U), G crackle network, B soft swirl, A 1
Beam_Noise.blend: multiply into Beam_Core; scroll R at 2-4 tiles/s and G at -1 tile/s for two layers

Bolt_Core.channels: CG: R core, G halo, B built-in tail streak, A coverage
Bolt_Core.tint: weapon colour on G (Bolt, Rail, Flak tracer, BaseTurret); R stays white
Bolt_Core.notes: Head at +U. Use on a stretched billboard (length ~3x width) aligned to velocity.

Cryo_Burst.channels: CG: R shard ridges + glints + flash, G shard bodies, B frost mist, A coverage
Cryo_Burst.blend: Additive R/G; B alpha-blended pale mist
Cryo_Burst.notes: Flat on the ground at the hit point (or camera-facing for air targets).

Debris_Shards.channels: R hot edge (emission), G body alpha, B facet shading, A body alpha
Debris_Shards.blend: Alpha blend body (colour = dark tint * B) + additive emission from R
Debris_Shards.tint: body dark metal/rock (0.12-0.2); edge amber, fade the edge to 0 over the particle life
Debris_Shards.notes: Random frame per particle, rotate over life, gravity on. For flying chunks behind explosions.

Dust_Burst_SixWayNeg.use: ground hits (mortar landing, heavy footfalls, crawler emerge)
Dust_Burst_SixWayNeg.channels: R light from left (-X), G light from bottom (-Y), B light from front (camera side), A emissive temperature 0..1 (map through a fire gradient)
Dust_Burst_SixWayNeg.blend: Alpha blend (straight alpha in Pos.A); lighting = sum of the six maps weighted by the squared light direction in billboard space; emission = gradient(Neg.A) * intensity added on top
Dust_Burst_SixWayNeg.tint: smoke albedo dark grey-brown (0.15-0.25); dust: tan (0.45, 0.38, 0.3); fire gradient on Neg.A

Dust_Burst_SixWayPos.use: ground hits (mortar landing, heavy footfalls, crawler emerge)
Dust_Burst_SixWayPos.channels: R light from right (+X), G light from top (+Y), B light from back (behind the smoke, away from the camera), A alpha (straight)
Dust_Burst_SixWayPos.blend: Alpha blend (straight alpha in Pos.A); lighting = sum of the six maps weighted by the squared light direction in billboard space; emission = gradient(Neg.A) * intensity added on top
Dust_Burst_SixWayPos.tint: smoke albedo dark grey-brown (0.15-0.25); dust: tan (0.45, 0.38, 0.3); fire gradient on Neg.A

Energy_Impact.channels: CG: R flash + ring front + spark cores, G glow, B inner ring, A coverage
Energy_Impact.tint: weapon colour on G (Bolt/Laser/Rail hits); B can take a second colour
Energy_Impact.notes: Camera-facing at the hit point; pair with Shockwave_Distort at a small strength.

HeatHaze_Distort.layout: single, tiles in U and V
HeatHaze_Distort.channels: R,G UV offset x/y encoded 0.5 +- 0.5, B height (for a mask), A 1
HeatHaze_Distort.blend: Refraction pass; scroll V upward 0.3-0.6 tiles/s over hot spots, strength 0.004-0.01
HeatHaze_Distort.notes: Import as Default, sRGB off. Fade with a radial mask on the quad (vertex alpha).

Muzzle_Front.channels: CG: R core, G flame glow, B smoke (cannon rows; alpha-blend grey), A coverage
Muzzle_Front.tint: G per weapon: gun (1, 0.75, 0.35), cannon (1, 0.6, 0.22), flak white-amber (1, 0.85, 0.55), rail/plasma weapon colour; R stays white
Muzzle_Front.notes: Rows = Gun, Cannon, Flak, Rail/Plasma; columns = 4 random variants. Show 1-3 frames (50 ms), random column per shot, random roll for the front view.
Muzzle_Front.view: front: barrel axis through the centre (camera looks down it)

Muzzle_Side.channels: CG: R core, G flame glow, B smoke (cannon rows; alpha-blend grey), A coverage
Muzzle_Side.tint: G per weapon: gun (1, 0.75, 0.35), cannon (1, 0.6, 0.22), flak white-amber (1, 0.85, 0.55), rail/plasma weapon colour; R stays white
Muzzle_Side.notes: Rows = Gun, Cannon, Flak, Rail/Plasma; columns = 4 random variants. Show 1-3 frames (50 ms), random column per shot, random roll for the front view.
Muzzle_Side.view: side: barrel at U=0.05 V=0.5, firing towards +U

Plasma_Bolt.channels: CG: R core bar + hot streams, G mantle glow, B swirl bands and tendrils, A coverage
Plasma_Bolt.tint: plasma colour on G, a second (lighter) colour on B
Plasma_Bolt.notes: Head at +U (U 0.78); loops seamlessly every 16 frames.

Rocket_Exhaust.channels: CG: R core + shock diamonds, G flame (bright at the nozzle, cooling to the tip), B heat/smoke start (alpha-blend grey), A coverage
Rocket_Exhaust.blend: Additive (R, G); B optional alpha layer
Rocket_Exhaust.notes: Nozzle at U=0 centre, flame to +U: put the quad behind the rocket with +U opposite to velocity.

Scorch_Decal.channels: R soot opacity, G albedo lightness (char 0.08 to ash 0.4), B ember emission mask, A ember fade threshold (an ember is lit while A > fade, fade 0 to 1 over the decal life)
Scorch_Decal.blend: URP Decal Projector or a ground quad (alpha blend): albedo = G * soot tint, alpha = R * fade-out; emission = B * step(fade, A) * ember colour (1, 0.35, 0.08) * 3
Scorch_Decal.notes: Pick a random cell and rotation per impact. Embers out in ~2 s, soot fades over ~8 s.

Shockwave_Distort.channels: R,G UV offset x/y encoded 0.5 +- 0.5 (+Y up), B ring mask, A 1
Shockwave_Distort.blend: Refraction pass: sample _CameraOpaqueTexture at screenUV + (RG*2-1) * B * strength (0.02-0.05)
Shockwave_Distort.notes: Import as Default, sRGB off, NOT as a Normal Map (Unity would drop B). Scale the quad outward like the shockwave ring; fade strength to 0.

Shockwave_Ring.channels: CG: R sharp front, G soft inner glow, B dusty breakup, A coverage
Shockwave_Ring.blend: Additive (energy) or alpha-blend B as a dust ring
Shockwave_Ring.tint: weapon colour on G; dust tan on B
Shockwave_Ring.notes: Scale the quad from ~0.2 to full size with an ease-out over 0.25-0.4 s; flat on the ground for ground hits, camera-facing for air bursts.

Smoke_Linger_SixWayNeg.channels: R light from left (-X), G light from bottom (-Y), B light from front (camera side), A emissive temperature 0..1 (map through a fire gradient)
Smoke_Linger_SixWayNeg.blend: Alpha blend (straight alpha in Pos.A); lighting = sum of the six maps weighted by the squared light direction in billboard space; emission = gradient(Neg.A) * intensity added on top
Smoke_Linger_SixWayNeg.tint: smoke albedo dark grey-brown (0.15-0.25); dust: tan (0.45, 0.38, 0.3); fire gradient on Neg.A

Smoke_Trail.channels: R lighting from the ribbon's top edge (0..1), G puff noise, B unused, A density
Smoke_Trail.blend: Alpha blend (premultiply in shader: rgb = tint*R*A)
Smoke_Trail.tint: smoke grey (0.35, 0.34, 0.33); fade the end of the trail with vertex alpha
Smoke_Trail.notes: Tile mode in U (~1 tile per 2 m); scroll slowly so the trail churns.

Spark_Burst.channels: CG: R spark cores + flash, G glow, A coverage
Spark_Burst.tint: hot amber (1, 0.6, 0.2) for shells; weapon colour for energy hits
Spark_Burst.notes: Pivot = impact point (U 0.5, V 0.42 from the bottom). Pair with mesh/GPU sparks using Spark_Streaks.

Spark_Streaks.channels: CG: R core, G glow, A coverage
Spark_Streaks.tint: amber (1, 0.6, 0.2) or weapon colour; fade R and G with particle life
Spark_Streaks.notes: Head at +U. Stretched Billboard render mode, speed scale ~0.05, random row per particle (Texture Sheet Animation, rows mode, random row).

Tesla_Arcs.channels: CG: R core (main + branches), G glow (+ end flares), B branches only, A coverage
Tesla_Arcs.notes: Each cell runs from U=0.02 to U=0.98 at V=0.5: stretch a quad between muzzle and target; pick a random frame per discharge or play at 20 fps for a crackling stream.

Trail_Noise.layout: single, tiles in U and V
Trail_Noise.channels: R ridged strands, G soft wisps (0.5 mean), B unused, A 1
Trail_Noise.blend: multiply into a trail or beam (scroll U at 1-3 tiles/s)

Trail_Ribbon.channels: CG: R core, G glow, A coverage
Trail_Ribbon.notes: U=0 head (newest point), U=1 tail. If Unity's trail runs the other way set the material tiling X to -1. Multiply with Trail_Noise scrolled along U for a living trail.
